item.title: Qereqeretabua says don't rush Constitution Bill
item.description: Temalesi Vono , Vijay Narayan · 04/11/2026 National Federation Party MP and Assistant Minister for Foreign Affairs, Lenora Qereqeretabua says the party believes more time is needed to consider the proposed Constitution Amendment Bill.
item.content:encoded:
Temalesi Vono , Vijay Narayan · 04/11/2026

National Federation Party MP and Assistant Minister for Foreign Affairs, Lenora Qereqeretabua says the party believes more time is needed to consider the proposed Constitution Amendment Bill.

When approached by fijivillage News on her stance, Qereqeretabua says the process should not be rushed, arguing that Fiji should not replace a Constitution imposed on the country by imposing another without allowing sufficient time for proper consideration.

When asked on whether he will vote for or against the Bill, NFP MP and Minister for Defence Pio Tikoduadua says the people will know when the vote takes place on the Constitution Amendment Bill.

SODELPA MP, Ifereimi Vasu says he is still discussing the party's position on the proposed Constitution Amendment Bill, despite the party directing its MPs to vote against the Bill.

When approached for his views, Vasu says he is continuing to consider the matter and will discuss it further with the party before a collective decision is made.

item.title: Ditoka says Fiji serious about concerns raised in US Trafficking In Persons Report
item.description: Minister for Foreign Affairs, Sakiasi Ditoka stresses that no individual or organisation should be considered beyond the reach of Fiji's laws because of their economic contribution, investment activities or employment of Fijian citizens. Ditoka says while questions in the US Trafficking In Persons Report for Fiji on INTERPOL Red Notices for some leaders of Grace Road Group not being honoured by Fi
item.content:encoded:
Minister for Foreign Affairs, Sakiasi Ditoka stresses that no individual or organisation should be considered beyond the reach of Fiji's laws because of their economic contribution, investment activities or employment of Fijian citizens.

Ditoka says while questions in the US Trafficking In Persons Report for Fiji on INTERPOL Red Notices for some leaders of Grace Road Group not being honoured by Fiji and the status of investigations are matters that must be addressed by the competent law enforcement and prosecutorial authorities, the allegations must be properly investigated, due process respected and any determination of criminal responsibility made on the evidence and in accordance with the law.

He says the protection of employment and legitimate economic activity is an important consideration for any Government, but it cannot be used to excuse criminal conduct where such conduct is established.

Ditoka adds that as to the investigation report commissioned by the Coalition Government, he believes the responsible authorities are best placed to clarify its status and any findings that may properly be disclosed.

He says it would be inappropriate for him to speculate on operational decisions, the status of individual investigations or matters that may be subject to legal proceedings.

However he stresses that the Government of Fiji takes the issue of human trafficking, including sexual exploitation, forced labour and the exploitation of vulnerable women and children, very seriously.

Ditoka says these are serious criminal offences and violations of human dignity, and there should be no misunderstanding about the Government's commitment to combating them.

The Foreign Affairs Minister says the United States is one of Fiji's most important development partners, and the longstanding bilateral relationship is one that Fiji values greatly.

He says Fiji's cooperation extends across development assistance, security, economic engagement and other areas of mutual interest.

Ditoka says they therefore attach considerable importance to the assessments and concerns raised by the United States Government, including those contained in its 2026 Trafficking In Persons Report.

He adds combating human trafficking requires coordinated action across several agencies with distinct statutory responsibilities.

These include the Fiji Police Force, immigration authorities, the Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions and the relevant ministries responsible for labour, social welfare and child protection.

The Minister says the challenges are not confined to law enforcement alone.

He says trafficking can involve complex criminal networks, cross-border movements, vulnerable individuals who may be reluctant or afraid to come forward, and circumstances where exploitation is difficult to identify or prove.

Ditoka says effective investigations require specialised skills, cooperation between agencies and, frequently, assistance from international partners.

Ditoka says the protection of victims must remain central to our national response.

He says those who have suffered exploitation should be treated with dignity and provided with appropriate assistance, irrespective of their nationality.

Ditoka says on the specific question of funding and support arrangements, the relevant ministries should provide a clear account of the resources currently available, the challenges they face and the additional measures that may be necessary.

item.title: Police urged to uphold unity, fairness and public trust this Diwali
item.description: Diwali celebrations at Police Headquarters have reminded officers of the importance of unity, fairness and trust in building a safer and more stable Fiji. Commissioner of Police Rusiate Tudravu says every positive action by a member of the Fiji Police Force contributes to a safer and more stable country.
item.content:encoded:
Diwali celebrations at Police Headquarters have reminded officers of the importance of unity, fairness and trust in building a safer and more stable Fiji.

Commissioner of Police Rusiate Tudravu says every positive action by a member of the Fiji Police Force contributes to a safer and more stable country.

In his address to officers during the celebrations, Tudravu says the light of Diwali reminds them that even a small light can make a difference in darkness.

Reflecting on this year's theme, “Lighting the Path to Stability, Growth and Unity,” Tudravu stressed the importance of officers working together as one force.

He says the Fiji Police Force must bring light where there is uncertainty, reassurance where there is fear, fairness where there is disagreement and hope to people facing difficulties.

Tudravu also reminded officers to continue upholding the trust placed in them by the people they serve.

The Fiji Police Force has extended its well wishes to everyone for a joyous, safe and prosperous Diwali.

item.title: Vunato dump fire could take three weeks to extinguish as residents raise concerns
item.description: Residents in Lautoka continue to raise concerns about smoke from the Vunato Rubbish Dump, with rubbish dumping concerns also continuing as the Lautoka City Council say it will take two to three weeks before it is fully extinguished Residents have raised concerns about the impact of the thick smoke on surrounding communities, with some reporting breathing difficulties.
item.content:encoded:
Residents in Lautoka continue to raise concerns about smoke from the Vunato Rubbish Dump, with rubbish dumping concerns also continuing as the Lautoka City Council say it will take two to three weeks before it is fully extinguished

Residents have raised concerns about the impact of the thick smoke on surrounding communities, with some reporting breathing difficulties.

Speaking to fijivillage News, Lautoka resident and journalism student Rishika Nair says the situation remains unchanged, with smoke still affecting the area.

Another resident says the smoke has continued to spread into nearby areas, affecting people living around the landfill.

The resident says similar incidents have occurred at the dump around the same time in previous years, raising concerns about the recurring problem .

Meanwhile, Lautoka City Council Head of Service Shalend Singh says the National Fire Authority has been assisting the Council since yesterday afternoon and has assured its support.

Singh says the Council has managed to prevent the fire from spreading and is currently working to extinguish fires in two sections of the landfill.

He says given the magnitude of the fire, it will take two to three weeks before it is fully extinguished.

However, Singh says smoke levels are expected to decrease in the coming days as firefighting operations continue around the clock, with Council teams working in two 12-hour shifts.

He says an excavator has also been engaged to assist with the operation.

Singh says the Council has distributed face masks to residents in Vunato, California and Veidogo settlements, with another distribution planned for this afternoon.

He is also urging CPRs not to enter the landfill while firefighting operations are underway.

Singh says the Minister and Permanent Secretary for Local Government are in regular contact with the Council and have assured their support.
